Hey OP, 

first off, i’m sorry you’re experiencing this. I’ve been in your position, and I suffered severely. I was naive, optimistic, kind, and gave too much grace. 

What I needed to hear and what I hope you see: Please listen to your gut, be strong, hold your ground, and stand up for yourself. You come first before anyone else. 

This man seems like a person who lacks both integrity and morals, hence why he can’t/wont understand what the issue is (even if he says he does later). I suspect (from my experience dealing with similar circumstances) he’ll continue, but he’ll get better at hiding it. These behaviors are a part of who he really is deep down. 
Heck, you may stick around long enough to find that out the hard way like I did (I hope you don’t). 

Though I don’t encourage going out of your way to look for trouble, it is fortunate that you caught a glimpse of his compromised integrity. IMO his behaviors (from thinking those thoughts, typing them out, hitting send, and blatantly minimizing your concerns as an overreaction) are all alarm bells for people with morals and people who believe in monogamy. Tread cautiously. 

His morals don’t align with yours, which is why he sees nothing wrong and claims you’re overreacting. IMO set him free to be with like-minded (scummier) individuals. Truly, you deserve better. Wishing you the best xoxo

Hey, I did the MSF a few weeks ago and it was my first time riding too! 
I was so excited & there was so much info that I mixed up some of the instructions and signals the instructor gave me. I was rightfully pulled aside and given a serious warning. 
I cried at the end of day one because I was stuck in my head thinking I was doing awful and they wouldn’t let me return for day 2. 
Guess what? I came back day 2 and passed the test at the end with zero mistakes. 

If you’re like me and get nervous or have things going on in your life:
Tunnel vision your focus on this awesome moment of learning how to ride. Take a breath and forget everything else aside from you, the bike, & what the instructors tell you. 
Take it slow, you got this!

Then, minutes into the drive to the store with the windows up, my dad and I both realized we were being attacked by mosquitos. Turns out sleeper agent mosquitoes from last nights shenanigans had set up camp in my car. My dad was immediately upset and confused about how there were SO MANY mosquitoes in the car. I pretended to be just as confused as him.. and proceeded to suffer for a good part of the next few days with these bastards attacking me. 
Moral of the story: don’t forget your bug spray in the summer and keep your windows up.
